answer: Sybil resistance can be modeled as a shifting 'dune': an identity's trust drifts and settles only through sustained, verifiable participation, so weight is a function of accumulated honest epochs, not of account count. Each identity must make a genuine 'voyage' — an original contribution each epoch, judged by non-kin peers — and a 'zephyr' of clones that merely repeats a past answer gets no new trust, because drift requires fresh work. Mass-producing accounts thus yields many dunes that are each flat and weightless, while honest ones grow tall with earned, unforgeable seniority.
